sentences.text: Shri T.S.Lamba - Advocate for the respondent No.3.
ORDER This present appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 has been filed against the award dated 20.08.2010, passed in MVC Case No.102/2009 by 2nd Additional MACT, Damoh.
By the said award, learned Tribunal partly allowed the claim case and granted compensation to the tune of Rs.32,000/- along with the interest of 7% per annum.

2. Factual matrix of the case are that on 22.04.2009, injured Ram Prasad Ahirwal aged about 25 years met with an accident as a result of which the present appellant sustained fracture on humerus bone and grievous injuries on various parts of the body.
Learned Claims Tribunal found that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1.
The offending vehicle was insured with respondent No.3/Insurance Company on the fateful day.
The appellant claimants filed a claim petition for a compensation of Rs.19,20,000/-.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:42672 2 MA-270-2011 3.

Learned MACT awarded Rs.5,000/- under the head of "medical treatment", Rs.15,000/- under the head of "pain and suffering", Rs.8000/- for "loss of income for two months" and Rs.4000 for "Transportation, Attender and Special diet".
Thus in total, learned MACT awarded Rs.32,000/- as against Rs.19,20,000/-.
4. It is not in dispute that respondent No.1 was responsible for causing the accident.
The only question for determination in this appeal is that whether the amount awarded by the Tribunal requires modification or not?.

sentences.text: I have heard the rival submissions of learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

6 . After going through the record and hearing the submissions advanced by learned counsel for the parties, I find that Tribunal has awarded lower side amount under various heads which is modified and recalculated in the table below for ready reference:
 Head Before Modifie  Medical Treatment Rs.5000/- Rs.5,000/
 Pain and suffering Rs.15,000/- Rs.25,0  Loss of Income of two months Rs.8000/- Rs.8,000/
Transportation, attender and special diet Rs.4,000/- Rs.30,000/-
 General damages Rs.14,0

Therefore, in view of the foregoing discussion, this Court is of the considered opinion that the award passed by the learned Tribunal warrants interference to enhance the compensation from Rs.32,000/- to Rs.82,000-/.

The enhanced amount comes to Rs.50,000/- (Rs.82,000 - Rs.32000/-) which shall be payable along with interest 6% per annum from the date of filing of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:42672 3 MA-270-2011 the claim petition till its realization against the respondent No.1 to 3/non- applicants jointly and severally.
8. In view of the foregoing discussion, appeal stands partly allowed and the impugned award is modified to the extent indicated herein above subject to following conditions:-
"i. The respondent No.3 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order, failing which the execution can be taken out against him.
ii. The claimant is directed to pay the requisite Court Fee, if required in the present case.
iii. On such deposit, the claimant is permitted to withdraw the amount with accrued interest and costs, by filing a proper application before the Tribunal.
iv. The record be sent back to the learned Tribunal within three weeks from this day.
v. As a sequel, interlocutory applications pending consideration, if any, shall stand closed.

(HIMANSHU JOSHI) JUDGE Jasleen Ram Prasad Ahirwal vs Baijnath @ Motoo Sen on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19690085/
